featured_reviews.name: Neelachandra Tawde
featured_reviews.review_text: Sassoon Dock, with its rich history, cultural significance, and bustling fishing activity, offers a glimpse into Mumbai's maritime heritage. As a vibrant and dynamic space, it continues to be an integral part of the city's life, serving as a testament to the coexistence of tradition and modernity. Whether for its historical value, its thriving fishing community, or its cultural vitality, Sassoon Dock stands as an enduring symbol of Mumbai's coastal legacy and its deep-rooted connection with the Arabian Sea.

featured_reviews.name: rajesh jaiswar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sassoon Dock Jetty, located in Colaba, is one of Mumbai’s oldest and most active jetties, offering a real glimpse into the city’s fishing and maritime life. Early mornings are the best time to visit, as you can see fishermen unloading their fresh catch, boats docking, and the local fish market coming alive with energy. The atmosphere is bustling and full of authentic coastal charm.

The jetty area has improved over time, with better cleanliness and organization. The view of the Arabian Sea and the colorful fishing boats make it a great spot for photography and exploring Mumbai’s heritage side. It’s also known for its connection to the Sassoon Dock Art Project, where murals and street art add a creative touch to the surroundings.

Visitors should be prepared for some fishy smells and wet floors, but the experience is truly worth it for those wanting to see Mumbai’s working waterfront up close.

Overall, Sassoon Dock Jetty is a lively, historic, and culturally rich spot that reflects the true coastal spirit of Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Shaibaz Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sassoon Dock is a historic and bustling fish market located in Mumbai, India. Named after the prominent Sassoon family, who were influential in the development of Mumbai during the British colonial era, this dock has been a vital hub for the city's fishing industry for over a century.

Key features and highlights of Sassoon Dock include:

1. Fishing Hub: Sassoon Dock is one of Mumbai's oldest fishing docks and continues to play a crucial role in the seafood industry. It serves as a primary landing point for fishermen who bring in their catch from the Arabian Sea.

2. Vibrant Fish Market: The area around Sassoon Dock is teeming with activity, especially in the early morning when the day's catch is unloaded and sold. The market is a vibrant and colorful scene with a wide variety of seafood on display, including fish, crabs, prawns, and more.

3. Local Culture: Visiting Sassoon Dock provides a unique glimpse into the local fishing culture of Mumbai. It's an opportunity to witness the daily routines and traditions of the fishermen and fisherwomen who depend on this livelihood.

4. Photography Destination: The visual spectacle of Sassoon Dock, with its bustling market and picturesque boats, has made it a popular spot for photographers and tourists. The vibrant chaos and the play of light and shadow create captivating scenes for photography enthusiasts.

5. Heritage Value: Sassoon Dock is a heritage site that reflects Mumbai's history as a bustling port city. The architecture of the dock and its surroundings showcase a blend of British colonial and local architectural styles.

6. Conservation Efforts: In recent years, there have been efforts to modernize and improve the facilities at Sassoon Dock while also addressing environmental concerns. Initiatives to promote sustainable fishing practices and reduce the dock's ecological footprint have gained attention.

Sassoon Dock is not just a place of economic significance but also a cultural and historical landmark in Mumbai. It offers a sensory-rich experience for visitors, whether they are interested in the seafood trade, photography, or simply wish to immerse themselves in the vibrant local atmosphere.

featured_reviews.name: SWAPNIL PATIL
featured_reviews.review_text:
We bought fish and mutton today.
Fish size was big and was fresh but mutton was not good.
We bought mutton from pakeezah mutton shop. I had been to this shop second time as first time mutton given was fresh.
Today's experience was very bad and I vow will not visit this shop again.
Mutton was not fresh at all and I had chosen the leg piece but they fool you right in front and give you something else. It was back bone piece and little  flesh. It took 12 whistles in cooker to cook this mutton and still it was not cooked properly.
I got 250 gms out of which flesh part would be just 50 to 70 gnms and rest all bones.
